items.title: The name
items.text: ThreeSixty Group bought the brand from Toys “R” Us in October 2016 and has run a flagship at 30 Rockefeller Plaza since November 16, 2018.[^26][^29] In September 2026 the company listed stores in New York, Paris (inside Galeries Lafayette), Milan and Beijing, and opened a storefront on Amazon.[^30]

items.title: The trademark
items.text: In 2003 the name was used under a perpetual license from the F.A.O. Schwarz Family Foundation, which received royalties.[^1] In 2016 Toys “R” Us still described what it held as “the exclusive right and license to use the FAO SCHWARZ trademarks.”[^25] Whether that arrangement continues under ThreeSixty Group is **unknown** to us.

items.title: FAO Inc.
items.text: The parent renamed itself Children’s Books & Toys, Inc. in February 2004, as the sale agreement required, told shareholders to expect nothing and filed to end its SEC registration in November 2004.[^8][^32]

items.title: Zany Brainy
items.text: The 89 remaining stores were liquidated from December 2003.[^7][^14]

items.title: The Right Start
items.text: The business that had bought FAO Schwarz was itself sold out of the bankruptcy to Hancock Park Capital, one of FAO Inc.’s shareholders, for about **$5.4M**.[^8]

items.title: 767 Fifth Avenue
items.text: The store left the General Motors Building on July 15, 2015.[^22] What occupies the space now is not in our sources.

items.title: The last corporate owner
items.text: Toys “R” Us, which owned FAO Schwarz from 2009 to 2016, declared bankruptcy itself not long after selling it.[^29]

items.title: The piano and one of the people
items.text: The floor piano went into the new store, and replicas were on sale for $128 in 2018.[^29] David Niggli, who had spent 15 years at F.A.O. Schwarz before becoming president of the FAO Schwarz subsidiary in 2002, was the brand’s chief merchandising officer in 2018 and still held that title in 2026.[^1][^29][^30]

nodes.owner: Peter L. Harris and Peter C. Morse
nodes.what: A management buyout. The flagship moves to 767 Fifth Avenue.[^9]
The Dutch retailer KBB buys the company and is itself taken over by Vendex International in 1998.[^9]
Buys 23 stores, the catalog and the website with notes and preferred stock.[^1]
Files on January 13, emerges on April 23, files again on December 4.[^1][^7]
Buys the name, the catalog, the website and two stores from the estate.[^8]
Runs the Fifth Avenue store until July 15, 2015 and puts the name on private-label toys.[^20][^21][^22]
Opens a new flagship at 30 Rockefeller Plaza in November 2018.[^26][^29]
